samples.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently breaks the `expectLoss`-before-`remove` invariant the store relies on, turning an archive into an outright delete of unsent work
samples.evidence: `DurableLossWatch` is the ONLY production caller of `expectLoss` (`packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:282`; grep for `expectLoss` finds no other non-test call site). `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` reads that latch at `packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771` and only writes an archive when it is set (`if (record && losing)` at line 791), documented at lines 735-737 as "The latch is set from the `LocalChangesDropped` handler ... so the flag is always in place by the time the removal arrives." This delta wraps the subscription in `try { ... } catch { console.warn(...) }` for exactly the case the new comment cites — an SDK where `subscribe('local-changes-dropped')` throws `Unsupported event type`. On such an SDK the handler is never registered, yet the SDK still calls `store.remove()` on its three loss paths, so the removal takes the `losing === false` branch: snapshot, header and change log are deleted with no archive, `listRecoverableWork` has nothing to list, and the user's unreconciled edits are gone with only a console warning. Before this change the throw was loud (it crashed the subtree, so the document was not editable and nothing was silently deleted); after it, editing continues over a store whose loss path now deletes. Fix belongs on the new code: when the loss subscription specifically cannot be installed, the durable store must not be handed to the client as an archiving store (e.g. disable persistence / report undurable) rather than just warning. Confidence is medium only because node_modules is not installed here, so I could not confirm whether @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22 emits this event — but the diff's own justification asserts it may not.

samples.summary: A swallowed `persist-disabled` subscription leaves the durability chip reporting "Saved to this device" for a document the SDK has stopped persisting
samples.evidence: `reportPersistDisabled()` is the only thing that latches durability off for the SDK-gave-up case; consumers read it via `useDocumentDurability()` (`packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-document-context.ts`, rendered by the sync-status chip — see `packages/frontend/tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:659` and `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-tooltip.ts:34`). With the new `watch()` helper a `subscribe('persist-disabled')` that throws is reduced to a `console.warn`, so the chip keeps asserting the document is saved locally while it is not — the opposite of the in-diff comment's claim that "an SDK that cannot report a lapse costs the chip its certainty". The certainty is exactly what is kept. The default when the event cannot be watched should be "not durable", not "durable".

samples.summary: The new "only a 404 may reach the workspace fallback" rule misses `fetchDocument`'s own non-HttpError not-found throw
samples.evidence: `fetchDocument` throws a plain `new Error("Document not found")` at packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:53 when the server answers OK with an empty/null body. `offerRecoverableWork` now tests `err instanceof HttpError && err.status === 404`, so that genuinely-gone case is classified as "could not confirm the document is gone" and the archive is never offered back — the work stays archived every session instead of being handed to the user. Impact is small (the archive is preserved, not lost), but the guard's stated contract ("a 404 is the document being gone") does not cover this second not-found representation.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `DurableLossWatch` at packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:280-285 registers the `local-changes-dropped` handler through `watch()` (lines 269-278), which swallows a throw into `console.warn`. That handler is the ONLY production caller of `expectLoss` (line 282; all other grep hits are test files), and `expectLoss` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739-741) is the only writer of `expectedLosses` (declared line 354). `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` reads that latch at line 771 and writes the archive only under `if (record && losing)` at line 791, while deleting snapshot/header/changes unconditionally at lines 809-811. The only `ARCHIVES ... put` in packages/frontend/src is line 802, so there is no fallback archiving path. The invariant is explicitly documented at lines 735-737 ("the flag is always in place by the time the removal arrives"). If the subscription throws (the exact case the new comment at lines 260-267 cites), the SDK-driven loss path silently deletes unreconciled work with only a console warning. I could not refute on unreachability: node_modules is absent so the 0.7.22 SDK's event support (packages/frontend/package.json:99) is unverifiable, and an event-name mismatch on a store-capable SDK reproduces the loss. This sits in the blast-radius lane as an invariant another module relies on, violated at a site outside the changed file.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The `watch()` helper at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:269-278 swallows any throw from `subscribe()` into a `console.warn`, and it wraps the `persist-disabled` subscription at :292-296 whose handler is the ONLY caller of `reportPersistDisabled()` (grep shows the symbol only in this file, the context interface at durable-document-context.ts:39, and test stubs). `persistDisabled` is the sole third conjunct of `durable` at :181, `durable` is published by `useDocumentDurability()` (durable-document-context.ts:74-76), read at use-sync-status.ts:75 and passed to `deriveSyncState`, which maps `durable ? 'saved-locally' : 'not-saved'` (sync-state.ts:85) and renders as "Saved to this device" (sync-status-chip.tsx:48). So when the subscription fails — the exact scenario the in-file comment at :260-267 says is expected on the pinned SDK 0.7.22 (package.json:66,99), which throws `ErrInvalidArgument 'Unsupported event type'` — the latch never arms and the chip keeps promising local durability, the opposite of the stated invariant at :90-108 that over-reporting durability is the one direction this feature must not fail in. No other producer sets the latch: `writesFailing`/`outOfSpace` only arm on store write failures (:148-158), which never occur once the SDK stops calling the store. I could not construct a counterexample (node_modules absent, so I cannot show SDK 0.7.22 lacks the persist-disable behaviour itself), and the invariant is consumed in modules outside the diff, so it stays in the blast-radius lane.
